note: Machine-readable registry. Source of truth = component-rules/<id>.md frontmatter (schema in component-rules/README.md). Regenerate with scripts/build-manifest.py.

components.summary: Vertically stacked, expandable sections that reveal or hide long content to keep a dense view scannable.

replaces: custom stacked 'ver más' blocks without a shared pattern

not_to_confuse_with.why: Collapsible is a single region; Accordion is multiple stacked sections
Tabs switch views; Accordion stacks disclosable content

motion.enter: Expand — panel animates grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr (data-state=open), revealing content in flow; the chevron rotates 180deg.
motion.exit: Collapse — the same grid-template-rows transition reversed (1fr → 0fr); chevron rotates back to 0.
motion.stateChange: Content height via grid-template-rows (var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-default)); chevron rotate 180deg (transform, var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-expressive)); trigger label color on hover/focus (var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-default)).
motion.easing: --ease-default (expand/collapse + trigger color), --ease-expressive (chevron rotation — the spatial move)
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). The panel snaps open/closed and the chevron flips instantly; disclosure still works because state is conveyed by aria-expanded + the rotated chevron, not motion alone.
motion.constraints: The grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr technique is the DS's sanctioned CSS-only height animation (no JS scrollHeight measurement) — the one place a size-like property is animated. Bottom spacing rides a zero-height ::after spacer, never animated padding. Keep the chevron a transform (Expressive) and the label color an effect (Standard) — don't cross the curves.
relatedPatterns: Standard-vs-Expressive split (effect color on --ease-default, spatial chevron on --ease-expressive)

components.summary: An inline, persistent contextual message that stays in the page flow until the user resolves or dismisses it.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Snackbar is floating + ephemeral; Alert is inline + persistent
Alert Dialog blocks and demands a choice; Alert coexists with content
Badge is a compact read-only status marker; Alert is a full contextual message

motion.enter: none — Alert is inline and persistent; it appears with the page, no entrance animation.
motion.exit: none — dismissal via .alert-close removes it immediately; no exit animation.
motion.stateChange: .alert-close fades opacity (.7→1) and shows a currentColor state-layer background on hover; focus ring on :focus-visible.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0); the close-button hover fade becomes instant. Nothing else moves.
motion.constraints: Inline/persistent — never animate it like an overlay; animate opacity/background only on the close affordance. Meaning must not rely on motion or color alone (pair with title/icon).

components.summary: A layout primitive that locks content to a fixed width:height ratio while the width stays fluid — for media, thumbnails, and embeds.

replaces: padding-bottom percentage hacks for intrinsic ratio boxes

not_to_confuse_with.why: Avatar is a fixed person circle; Aspect Ratio is a fluid-width media box
Skeleton is the loading placeholder; Aspect Ratio reserves the final media's shape

motion.enter: none — a layout primitive; it reserves space so media can load without shift, but it does not animate in.
motion.stateChange: none — it is the native CSS aspect-ratio property on a div, with no interactive states or transitions of its own.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific behavior — the ratio box never animates; reserving space up front is itself the anti-jank measure.
motion.constraints: Never animate the ratio box or its dimensions — its whole purpose is to hold a stable shape and prevent layout shift while media loads. Any motion belongs to the media child (e.g. a Skeleton→image fade), not to the wrapper.
relatedPatterns: No motion — stable layout prevents reflow/shift as assets load (motion.md performance: never animate layout)

source.css: layout primitive — no dedicated css/components file; uses the native CSS aspect-ratio property

components.summary: A compact file row showing an icon/thumbnail, name and metadata, with an optional remove action, upload progress, or error state.

not_to_confuse_with.why: input chips are compact removable tokens; Attachment is a file row with metadata + progress
the <input type=file> does the picking; Attachment displays the result

motion.enter: none — rows appear in the list statically.
motion.exit: none — removing a row (attachment-remove) is immediate.
motion.stateChange: Uploading state animates the progress bar width (.attachment-progress-bar); the remove control is a standard icon-btn with its own hover/press.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0); the upload progress bar snaps to its width instead of animating. Upload status is still conveyed by the numeric/aria state.
motion.constraints: The small 4px meter transitions width — a deliberate exception to the transform-only rule; animate transform/opacity elsewhere. Don't animate row insertion/removal (keep the list stable).

components.summary: A circle showing a person's photo or initials over a brand tonal fill — identifies a person, never a non-person entity.

replaces: hardcoded-gradient initial divs / ad-hoc profile circles

not_to_confuse_with.why: Badge is read-only status text; Avatar identifies a person
skeleton-circle is the loading placeholder for an avatar, not an avatar

motion.enter: none — the avatar is a static identity element.
motion.stateChange: none — avatar.css declares no transitions, hover states, or animations. Presence is shown with a static color dot (.avatar-badge / -online/-busy/-away/-offline) and stacking uses static negative margins + a surface ring.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific behavior — the avatar and its presence badge are already fully static.
motion.constraints: Do not animate an avatar — it is an identity marker, not a control. If a presence badge needs attention, convey it with color, never a pulsing/blinking loop (would risk the WCAG 2.3.1 >3 flashes/second threshold).
relatedPatterns: No motion — static identity element (motion.md: animate only for feedback/continuity/hierarchy)

components.summary: A quiet inline link with a leading chevron that returns to the parent view from a detail page — one step up, never a general-purpose action.

not_to_confuse_with.why: breadcrumb shows the whole trail and suits depth ≥2; back-link is one step to one known parent
a back link navigates; cancel, discard and close act on data or on an overlay
tabs switch between sibling views; this goes up a level

motion.enter: none — present with the page.
motion.stateChange: colour transitions on --duration-fast on hover; nothing moves.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global rule in css/base.css. A colour transition is not motion, so nothing is suppressed.
motion.constraints: Never slide the chevron on hover. The only approved hover transform in Embassy is translateY(-1px), and it is not for this.

components.summary: A read-only pill communicating an item's status, category, or a count — each color carries a fixed meaning; never interactive.

not_to_confuse_with.why: chips are interactive (filter/select/remove); a badge is read-only status
buttons act; a badge only informs
alert is a persistent inline message block; a badge is a compact status pill

motion.enter: none — always present (read-only status/category label).
motion.stateChange: The base badge is fully static (no transition). Only the link variant (a.badge) transitions opacity and fades to .85 on hover, with a 2px --color-focus focus-visible outline. An optional leading spinner inside a badge is a continuous Loading loop, not a badge state change.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css. No component-specific override. Note: a spinner embedded in a badge is a Loading-family loop (exempt category per guidelines/motion.md) and stops under reduced motion via the same global rule.
motion.constraints: Static by default — do not animate a status/category badge appearing or changing. Only the navigable a.badge earns a hover fade (opacity, compositor-safe).

components.summary: A hierarchy trail showing where the user is and letting them jump back to an ancestor.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Back Link is a single 'volver'; Breadcrumb is a multi-level trail
Navigation is primary wayfinding; Breadcrumb shows location
Pagination pages through a set; Breadcrumb shows hierarchy

motion.enter: none — the trail renders statically with the page.
motion.stateChange: Links transition text color on hover (transition: color .15s var(--ease-default, ease)) and add an underline. The collapse ellipsis, when a <button>, changes background on hover with no declared transition (instant).
motion.duration: hardcoded .15s on .breadcrumb-link — NOT a --duration-* token; should be --duration-fast
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). The hover color/underline applies instantly; navigation remains fully usable.
motion.constraints: Only text color animates (an effect → Standard easing) — correct; the underline is instant. No layout animation. Fix the hardcoded .15s to --duration-fast to satisfy the no-raw-ms rule (GOVERNANCE §13.3).
relatedPatterns: Feedback — hover color/underline signals a clickable ancestor
Hover micro-interaction (color change is an effect on Standard easing)

components.summary: A container that visually joins related buttons (or an input + addon) into one unit by collapsing shared borders and radii — it carries no selection state of its own.

tokens.radius: --radius-* inherited from the child buttons; inner corners collapse to 0
tokens.spacing: children share a single 1px border (no gap between joined members)

replaces: rows of adjacent buttons with hand-tuned radius overrides

not_to_confuse_with.why: segmented picks 1 of N with persistent selected state; button group has no selection
toggle-group holds stateful on/off toggles; button group holds plain actions

motion.enter: none — always present; the group is a layout wrapper only (joins children by collapsing inner radii/borders).
motion.stateChange: The group itself declares no transition — on focus-visible a child is raised via z-index: 1 (no animated property). All hover/press/focus motion is delegated to the child controls (see button.css → button.md: hover lift, press layer, focus ring).
motion.duration: none of its own — inherits --duration-fast from the child buttons.
motion.easing: none of its own — inherits --ease-default from the child buttons.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css. No component-specific override; children collapse their own motion.
motion.constraints: Never animate the radius/border collapse that joins members — it is a static structural style. Motion belongs to the child buttons, not the group.

components.summary: Triggers an action. Chosen by hierarchy (color) and density (size); exactly one primary action per context.

tokens.radius: --radius-* scaled by size class (sm→--radius-sm … xl→--radius-lg), written as var(--radius-button, <that token>). A brand theme with the `pildora` shape declares --radius-button: 9999px and every button becomes a pill at every size — that is the only way a button is ever a pill, and it is decided once at kickoff, never per screen (GOVERNANCE §4.2).

replaces: a flat 'action row' → map to a hierarchical button group

not_to_confuse_with.why: chips filter/select/represent input; buttons perform actions
segmented switches a view/mode; button acts once
badge is a read-only status; not interactive

motion.enter: none — always present (static control, not an overlay).
motion.stateChange: Hover: filled variants darken (primary→--color-primary-hover, secondary/elevated via color-mix) AND lift with transform: translateY(-1px); elevated also grows box-shadow (--btn-elevation→--btn-elevation-hover). Active/pressed: settle to translateY(0) + a 12% press layer (filter: brightness(.88/.92) on filled, surface-container-high on tertiary/icon, primary 16% on text). Focus-visible: 2px --color-focus ring + 4px --color-focus-ring.
motion.duration: --duration-fast (background/border-color/color/box-shadow). Transform (the lift/settle) uses a hardcoded .1s — should be tokenized to --duration-fast.
motion.easing: --ease-default for every property, including transform (this buildless CSS does NOT use --ease-expressive for the lift, unlike the retired Tailwind button.tsx described in guidelines/motion.md).
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific override — the lift/press simply collapse.
motion.constraints: Never animate layout (width/padding) — a button has intrinsic width. Only compositor-friendly props: transform (lift), plus color/shadow effects. --translateY(-1px) is the only approved transform effect; no scale-up/rotate on hover.

components.summary: A month-grid date/range picker with real month/year navigation — the base of the Date Picker, usable inline or docked in a popover, dialog, or sheet.

replaces: ad-hoc date pickers without an accessible grid

not_to_confuse_with.why: Select picks month/year or a bounded option; Calendar picks a specific day/range
Popover is the container; the Date Picker is Calendar docked inside one

motion.enter: none — the calendar grid renders in place. When shown inside a Date Picker the popover's entrance/exit is governed by date-picker.css, not calendar.css.
motion.exit: none (see enter — popover presentation lives in date-picker.css).
motion.stateChange: Day cells and nav buttons transition background-color on hover (transition: background-color .15s var(--ease-default, ease)); preset buttons transition background + border-color on the same timing. Month/year navigation is an instant JS re-render of the grid — no CSS transition. Selected/today/range states apply instantly via class swaps.
motion.duration: hardcoded .15s on .calendar-day, .calendar-nav-btn and .calendar-preset-btn — NOT --duration-* tokens; should be --duration-fast
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). Hover tints apply instantly; the month re-render is already instant, so navigation and selection stay fully legible.
motion.constraints: Hover feedback is background-color/border only (effect → Standard easing) — correct. Do NOT animate the month change: it is a full grid re-render and animating it would be layout thrash. Selection and range states are instant class swaps by design. Replace the hardcoded .15s values with --duration-fast to satisfy the no-raw-ms rule (GOVERNANCE §13.3).
relatedPatterns: Feedback — day/nav hover confirms the target (effect on Standard easing)
Visibility of system status — today/selected/range states (color, not motion)
Date Picker popover entrance belongs to date-picker.css (Popover/Dialog/Sheet presentation)

components.summary: A rich content panel that groups content and actions about a single subject on a surface.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Basic Card (item) is a compact row primitive; Full Card is a rich multi-part panel
Stat Card shows a single KPI; Full Card groups general content
specialized domain card; Full Card is generic

motion.enter: none — a static container with no CSS entrance
motion.stateChange: none — Card declares no transition. The three variants (.card outlined, .card-elevated shadow, .card-filled) are fixed at rest; there is no hover lift or shadow-grow.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). The component defines no motion of its own, so nothing extra to reduce.
motion.constraints: Card is a static surface — do not add a hover lift or shadow-grow (that is Button/Elevated behavior, GOVERNANCE §9; elevation is a fixed rest state here). If the card must be clickable, use Basic Card (item.css), which carries the interactive background/border state transition.
relatedPatterns: motion.md → Motion has a purpose (a static surface needs no motion)

components.summary: A scroll-snapping, browsable set of homogeneous items (images or cards) with prev/next controls — for secondary content that doesn't fit in one row.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Tabs switch between distinct panels; Carousel browses one homogeneous collection
Scroll Area is free scroll; Carousel snaps to discrete items with controls
compare options in a grid/Table, not a carousel

motion.enter: none — items are present in the scroll track from the start (no entrance animation).
motion.stateChange: Nav button background tint on hover (.carousel-btn:hover → --color-surface-variant); prev/next scroll the track via native scroll-behavior: smooth (scrollBy).
motion.duration: --duration-fast (nav button background); native smooth scroll for the track (no token).
motion.easing: --ease-default (nav button background); browser default for smooth scroll.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0); the same rule sets scroll-behavior: auto, so prev/next jump instantly instead of smooth-scrolling. If autoplay is ever added it must pause and honor reduced motion.
motion.constraints: No autoplay, no infinite loop, no drag physics; animate transform/opacity only; never animate the track's width/height — rely on native scroll. Controls disable at the ends rather than looping.

components.summary: Line, area, bar, and pie visualizations for dashboards and analytics — hand-drawn inline SVG + CSS conic-gradient, themed with the --chart-1..5 categorical palette.

replaces: static image charts, custom canvas, or charting libs with no theming

not_to_confuse_with.why: Stat Card shows one metric; Charts show a series/comparison/composition
Table gives exact per-row values; a chart shows the shape of the data

motion.enter: none — the SVG chart renders statically (no draw-on or grow-in animation).
motion.stateChange: On hover, .chart-dot grows its radius (r → 5.5) and .chart-bar dims (opacity → .82); the JS-positioned rich tooltip fades in/out via .chart-tooltip.is-visible (opacity 0↔1).
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0); hover feedback and the tooltip fade become instant. Values are still conveyed by the native <title> a11y fallback.
motion.constraints: No draw/brush/zoom/legend animation (out of scope for the buildless chart); animate opacity and the SVG r attribute only. The tooltip is pointer-events:none and must not trap focus.

components.summary: A native checkbox for selecting one or more options from a set — three states (unchecked / checked / indeterminate); the change applies on confirm, not instantly.

not_to_confuse_with.why: radio is exclusive single choice; checkbox is independent multi-select
switch applies instantly; checkbox applies on confirm
chips are inline toolbar filters; checkboxes are form-level selection

motion.enter: none — the control is always present
motion.stateChange: On :checked / :indeterminate the box fills --color-primary and its border goes transparent — a color effect (transition: background + border-color). Hover darkens the border to --color-on-surface. The ::after check glyph (and the indeterminate dash) has NO transition — it appears instantly. .checkbox-card transitions border-color + background-color on :has(input:checked)/hover.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No looping/essential motion; the checked fill still shows, just without the fade.
motion.constraints: Animate background/border-color only (effects, no layout). The check/dash glyph stays instant — don't add a draw/scale/fade to ::after. Never overshoot a color fill (Standard easing only).
relatedPatterns: motion.md → Hover & press micro-interactions (state-layer color change = effect, Standard easing)

components.summary: A compact, interactive element for filtering, selecting, or representing input — never for primary actions.

not_to_confuse_with.why: badge is read-only status; chip is interactive
segmented is single-select view switch; filter chips are usually multi-select
buttons act; chips filter/select/represent input

motion.enter: none — always present (static filter/input element).
motion.exit: none (an input chip being removed is a DOM removal, not an animated exit).
motion.stateChange: Hover/active: state layer via color-mix over the base — unselected on-surface 8%/12%, selected on-secondary-container 8%/12% over the container, elevated the same mixed over surface-container-low. Selected: fill flips to --color-secondary-container (transitions on background). Focus-visible: 2px --color-focus ring + 4px --color-focus-ring. Dragged: box-shadow lifts to --shadow-md.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific override.
motion.constraints: Only animate compositor-friendly effects (background/color state layer, box-shadow); no transform lift. Do not animate the height/padding-asymmetry change when an icon/remove slot appears.

components.summary: A single show/hide region toggled by any trigger — a minimal disclosure with one boolean state.

replaces: ad-hoc display:none toggles without transition or accessible state

not_to_confuse_with.why: Accordion is multiple stacked sections; Collapsible is a single region

motion.enter: Expand — the single region animates grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr (data-state=open), revealing its content in flow.
motion.exit: Collapse — the same grid-template-rows transition reversed (1fr → 0fr).
motion.stateChange: Content height via grid-template-rows only (transition grid-template-rows var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-default)). No chevron, no color transition — intentionally minimal so the trigger can be any element.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). The region snaps open/closed; state stays legible via aria-expanded on the trigger.
motion.constraints: Same sanctioned grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr CSS-only height animation as Accordion (no JS measurement). Collapsible deliberately styles nothing else that moves — don't add a chevron/label transition here (that distinction is what separates it from Accordion). Effect on Standard easing; never Expressive on a height change.

components.summary: A searchable single-select — a trigger button that opens a filterable Command list; pick one value from a long set by typing to narrow it.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Select has no typeahead; use it for short lists
Command runs commands / navigates (⌘K); Combobox picks a form value
chips represent multi-select tokens; Combobox is single-select

motion.enter: none — the panel is shown/hidden via a [hidden]/display toggle with no entrance animation (unlike the ⌘K Command Dialog, which slides up).
motion.stateChange: Trigger inherits btn-tertiary hover/focus transitions; combobox-check opacity 0→1 marks the selected option (instant, no transition declared); chevron is static.
motion.duration: none of its own (trigger uses button.css --duration-fast); the panel has no timed animation.
motion.easing: none of its own (trigger inherits button.css --ease-default).
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific motion to neutralize — the panel already appears instantly.
motion.constraints: Panel open/close is a display toggle. If an entrance is ever added, use transform/opacity + tokens (mirror the Command Dialog slideInUp) — never animate width/height.

components.summary: A searchable command palette / filterable list — substring-filtered items with arrow/Enter navigation and an empty state, optionally opened as a ⌘K Command Dialog.

not_to_confuse_with.why: Search queries app content/results; Command runs commands / navigates
Select picks one value from a short bounded list; Command is a searchable command surface
Combobox is a single-value form field built ON the Command filter; Command is the palette itself

motion.enter: Base Command: none (inline list, no entrance). Command Dialog (⌘K): scrim fadeIn + panel slideInUp (fade + upward translate) on open.
motion.exit: none — closing toggles [hidden]/display:none (no data-[state=closed] exit animation).
motion.stateChange: command-item[data-active=true] → surface-variant highlight as Arrow keys move through results (applied instantly, no transition declared); input focus is native; filtered items toggle [hidden].
motion.duration: HARDCODED .15s (scrim fadeIn) and .2s (panel slideInUp) — NOT --duration-* tokens (should map to --duration-normal / --duration-fast).
motion.easing: HARDCODED `ease` on both dialog animations — NOT an --ease-* token (should map to --ease-default / --ease-enter).
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). The ⌘K dialog appears without fade/slide; the active-item highlight is already instant.
motion.constraints: Animate transform/opacity only (slideInUp translate + scrim opacity). Keep the filtered-list re-render cheap; never animate the list height on filter.

components.summary: A cursor-anchored actions menu opened by right-click (or long-press) on an element — the same panel as Dropdown Menu, just a different trigger.

replaces: custom position:fixed context menus with ad-hoc z-index

not_to_confuse_with.why: Dropdown Menu opens from a visible trigger on click; Context Menu opens at the cursor on right-click
Navigation Menu moves between sections; Context Menu acts on an element

motion.enter: Panel scales + fades in on open, reusing Dropdown Menu's @keyframes dropdownIn (opacity 0→1, scale .96→1) — context-menu.css adds no motion of its own.
motion.exit: none defined in CSS — the panel is removed instantly on dismiss (known buildless gap vs. the Radix open/closed pair).
motion.stateChange: Item hover/focus background tint, inherited from the shared .dropdown-item styles.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0); the open scale/fade becomes instant.
motion.constraints: Reuses the Dropdown Menu panel — do not fork its motion; animate transform/opacity only. Positioned at the cursor by JS; no submenu support.

components.summary: The frame for a full-page creation or editing form — a large title above, and a footer that sticks to the bottom of the viewport so the save action is reachable no matter how long the form runs.

not_to_confuse_with.why: a dialog is for a short focused task that blocks; this is a full page for a long one
page-header names a view; create-header names an action in progress and pairs with the sticky footer
a bottom sheet is a mobile overlay for a secondary task, not the primary creation flow

motion.enter: none — the frame is present with the page.
motion.stateChange: The footer does not animate as it sticks; no shadow appears on scroll. The primary button's loading state follows button.css.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global rule in css/base.css.
motion.constraints: Do not animate the footer in and out on scroll direction. A save action that hides is worse than one that scrolls.

components.summary: An interactive table over static Table — column sort, text filter, row selection, column visibility, and slice pagination via initDataTable().

not_to_confuse_with.why: Table is static; Data Table adds sort/filter/selection/pagination
List is a simple vertical list, not a comparable-columns grid

motion.enter: none — the table renders in place; sorting, filtering and pagination re-slice rows instantly.
motion.exit: none — filtered-out or off-page rows are hidden via the [hidden] attribute, no exit animation.
motion.stateChange: All instant — no CSS transition is declared anywhere in data-table.css. The sort caret rotates 180deg (transform, descending) and gains full opacity when active; the sort button and rows change background/visibility with no timed transition; column-visibility toggles set display:none.
motion.duration: none — data-table.css declares no motion tokens
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (all transitions/animations neutralized to ~0). No component-specific behavior — nothing here animates in the first place, so state changes already read as instant.
motion.constraints: Sort/filter/paginate are instant state swaps by design — don't add row entrance/exit motion (a table reflowing on every sort is layout thrash). If feedback is ever wanted, animate opacity only on row show/hide, keep the caret a transform, and pull real --duration-*/--ease-* tokens rather than hardcoding.
relatedPatterns: Visibility of system status — the caret/aria-sort communicate sort direction without motion
Feedback (row hover) if ever added, as an effect on Standard easing

components.summary: A trigger button showing the chosen date, which opens a Calendar in a floating panel below it — the form and toolbar default, for when a permanent calendar would cost too much space.

replaces: ad-hoc date inputs with no accessible calendar

not_to_confuse_with.why: Calendar is the inline, always-visible grid for when date-picking is the main task; Date Picker docks that same grid behind a trigger
Select picks one value from a short fixed list; a date is a continuous range best chosen on a grid
combobox filters a list by typing; there is no list of dates to filter

motion.enter: The panel fades in and rises 4px on --duration-fast with --ease-default (`date-picker-in`).
motion.exit: Immediate. A closing overlay that lingers delays the next action.
motion.stateChange: The trigger follows .btn-tertiary's state layer; no motion of its own.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global rule in css/base.css — the transform and fade are suppressed and the panel appears immediately.
motion.constraints: Do not scale the panel on entry, and do not animate the calendar's contents separately. One 4px rise for the whole panel.

components.summary: A bordered block with an editable heading and a rich-text body — for long-form content the person writes in named, reorderable sections, not for a plain textarea.

not_to_confuse_with.why: form.css covers fields with fixed labels; here the label itself is content the person writes
an accordion collapses existing content for reading; this is an editing surface
a card groups content for display; this one is authored in place

motion.enter: A newly added section appears immediately. If it is animated, it is the shared list-item entrance on --duration-fast, never a bespoke one.
motion.exit: Immediate on delete, paired with an undo affordance — do not spend an animation softening a destructive act.
motion.stateChange: The delete button transitions background and colour on --duration-fast; the editor transitions its focus box-shadow on the same.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global rule in css/base.css. The opacity reveal of the delete button is a state change, not decoration, and must remain perceivable — under reduced motion it appears without a transition rather than not at all.

components.summary: A modal surface that interrupts the user for a focused task or a decision that must be resolved before continuing.

motion.easing: Currently HARDCODED `ease` on both keyframes. Intended tokens: --ease-enter for the scrim fade-in, --ease-exit for the (missing) exit; modal-close uses --ease-default.
motion.reducedMotion: Inherits the global prefers-reduced-motion rule in css/base.css (fadeIn/slideInUp durations collapse to ~0.01ms, so the Dialog appears instantly). No component-specific override.

components.summary: A 1px line that separates groups of equal-hierarchy content — the lightest separation in the system, no brand color, no elevation.
